stories.title: Sephora Relocates Meatpacking District Store with Long-Term Lease
stories.excerpt: Taconic Partners and Nuveen Real Estate signed a long-term lease with Sephora for approximately 4,200 square feet of ground-floor retail space at 401 W. 14th St. in Manhattan’s Meatpacking District. The current Meatpacking location on Ninth Avenue will be relocated to the new store, which is expected to open in the first quarter of 2027. Positioned adjacent to Apple’s Meatpacking District flagship, the location is at the center of one of Manhattan’s most prominent retail corners. “Sephora is a leading prestige beauty retailer and their move to 401 West 14th Street underscores the importance that a highly visible and trafficked location has on the establishment of a strong retail presence.” said Michael Adelstein, Vice President, Taconic Partners. “The Meatpacking District, and in particular the corner of 9th avenue and 14th street, is one of the most iconic and in-demand shopping destinations in the world. We expect that to continue as the 14th Street Plan, launched by NYC DOT in partnership with the Meatpacking & Union Square BIDs complete permanent transit, streetscape enhancements, and public space improvements in the coming years.” According to Cushman & Wakefield, retail availability in the Meatpacking District declined six percentage points year over year, the steepest contraction of any Manhattan submarket tracked by the firm, while average asking rents increased 10.3% year over year. At the corner of 14th Street and Ninth Avenue, 401 West 14th Street is approximately 65,000-square foot, mixed-use building located at the gateway to Manhattan’s historic Meatpacking District. Following acquisition of the building in 2005, Taconic assembled an award-winning design team including COOKFOX Architects to reposition the property into a neighborhood-defining retail and office opportunity. bullets: Sephora relocates Meatpacking District store to 401 W. 14th St., 4,200 sf, opens Q1 2027
Retail availability in Meatpacking District contracted 6 points YoY, steepest decline in Manhattan
NYC DOT 14th Street Plan underway; location adjacent to Apple flagship store
stories.summary: Sephora is relocating its Meatpacking District flagship from Ninth Avenue to a larger, more prominent ground-floor retail space at 401 W. 14th St. (4,200 sf) in partnership with Taconic Partners and Nuveen Real Estate, opening Q1 2027. The move signals confidence in the Meatpacking District as a top-tier retail destination despite—or because of—a steep 6-point YoY contraction in available retail space. The district is undergoing streetscape upgrades via NYC DOT's 14th Street Plan and benefits from proximity to Apple's flagship.
stories.impact: Retail space scarcity in Meatpacking District (steepest Manhattan decline) coupled with major anchor tenant expansion signals tight supply and strong demand fundamentals. This increases ground-floor retail rents and encourages mixed-use development with residential components above retail; developers should prioritize Meatpacking/Union Square West for new residential towers with street-level retail activation.

stories.title: Avatar Furnishes Bridge Loan on Fully Leased Santa Ana Warehouse
stories.excerpt: Avatar Financial Group LLC provided a $4.75-million bridge loan secured by a fully leased warehouse and distribution building in Santa Ana. The two-year, first-lien loan was originated at approximately 60% loan-to-value. The financing replaced two loans with one, retiring the property’s existing first mortgage along with a junior loan that had passed its maturity date. The tenant had invested substantially in its own build-out, and rent had commenced before the loan closed. After approximately 6 months of rental income, the sponsor intends to obtain long-term financing and repay Avatar’s bridge loan. “A lease that has just commenced doesn’t underwrite the same as one with a payment history behind it,” said T.R. Hazelrigg IV, Avatar’s president and co-founder. “A bank waits for that history to exist. Our job is deciding whether it will. At a 60% basis, with the tenant’s own money already in the space, that wasn’t a hard call.” The 18,876-square-foot light industrial facility at 4001 West Carriage Dr. sits on approximately 0.9 acres, less than two miles from Interstate 405 and State Route 55. The post Avatar Furnishes Bridge Loan on Fully Leased Santa Ana Warehouse appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Avatar Financial provides $4.75M bridge loan, Santa Ana warehouse, 60% LTV
18,876 sf light industrial property, 0.9 acres, near I-405 and SR-55
Two-year bridge to replace expired junior loan; tenant build-out complete, rent commenced
stories.summary: Avatar Financial Group originated a $4.75 million, two-year bridge loan secured by a fully leased light industrial warehouse and distribution building in Santa Ana (18,876 sf, 0.9 acres). The loan was structured at approximately 60% LTV and replaced two existing loans, including a junior mortgage past maturity. The tenant had invested substantially in its own build-out before rent commenced; the sponsor plans to obtain long-term financing and repay the bridge within approximately 6 months of rental income history.
stories.impact: Bridge lending appetite for newly stabilized industrial assets in Orange County reflects confidence in light industrial/logistics demand near major freeway corridors. This signals institutional lenders are willing to fund sub-stabilized assets with strong tenant capital at-risk; developers should accelerate lease-up timelines for last-mile distribution properties in the I-405/SR-55 corridor before financing windows tighten.

stories.title: George Comfort & Sons Refinances 200 Madison for $386M
stories.excerpt: George Comfort & Sons, and its partners Loeb Partners Realty and Jamestown, completed a $386-million refinancing of 200 Madison Ave., a 750,000-square-foot Grand Central district office tower. New York Life provided the five-year floating rate loan, structured with a three-year initial term and two 12-month extension options. Proceeds will be used to pay off 200 Madison’s existing debt and fund ongoing leasing. The refinancing follows an August agreement with Havas Health for a 15-year extension and headquarters expansion, which grew the global firm’s footprint to 254,118 square feet. Other notable office tenants include architecture practice Spectorgroup and boutique law firm BraunHagey & Borden. “This refinancing underscores the lending community’s confidence in office assets like 200 Madison Ave. that are defined by top-tier amenities, unrivaled location and strong sponsorship,” said George Comfort & Sons President and CEO Peter S. Duncan. Jonathan Estreich, Peter A. Duncan and Egor Petrov of Estreich & Company and Adam Spies, Adam Doneger and Willis Robbins of Newmark assisted in arranging the transaction. The post George Comfort & Sons Refinances 200 Madison for $386M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: George Comfort & Sons refis 200 Madison Ave., NYC office tower, $386M at floating rate
Havas Health expanded headquarters to 254,118 sf on 15-year extension in August
New York Life five-year floating loan; three-year initial + two 12-month extension options
stories.summary: George Comfort & Sons, partnered with Loeb Partners Realty and Jamestown, completed a $386 million refinancing of 200 Madison Ave., a 750,000-square-foot Grand Central office tower. New York Life provided a five-year floating-rate loan with a three-year initial term and two 12-month extension options. The refinance follows an August headquarters expansion agreement with Havas Health that grew its footprint to 254,118 sf on a 15-year extension.
stories.impact: Lender confidence in premium, fully leased office assets with strong sponsorship and anchor tenants remains intact despite floating-rate risk. However, floating-rate structures signal lenders expect rate volatility; developers should monitor whether future office refinancings shift to fixed-rate debt and whether Havas's expansion signals broader demand recovery in Midtown Manhattan office submarkets serving multinational corporates.

stories.title: Zurich Affiliate Acquires San Francisco Offices with Leasing Upside
stories.excerpt: Cushman & Wakefield has arranged the sale of 410 Townsend, a historic 78,455-square-foot office building in downtown San Francisco. An affiliate of Zurich Alternative Asset Management purchased the building for $47.4 million from New York Life Real Estate Investors and Bridgeton Holdings. Seth Siegel and Ryan Venezia of Cushman & Wakefield’s Northern California Capital Markets Team led the transaction. “410 Townsend is a compelling example of San Francisco’s rapid rebound and the opportunity to capitalize on the market’s strengthening fundamentals; this is the first ‘round trip’ for a San Francisco office building,” said Siegel. “Transactions like this demonstrate that investors are taking a closer look at San Francisco assets where the right combination of location, quality and basis can create meaningful opportunities.” Built in 1912, 410 Townsend features exposed brick and heavy timber construction while offering a range of modern amenities and flexible office layouts. With its current 65% occupancy, the property provides significant potential for additional leasing and value creation. bullets: Zurich Alternative Asset Management acquires 410 Townsend, San Francisco office, $47.4M
78,455 sf historic building, 65% occupied; first 'round trip' for SF office
Built 1912, exposed brick/heavy timber, significant leasing upside opportunity
stories.summary: An affiliate of Zurich Alternative Asset Management purchased 410 Townsend, a 78,455-square-foot historic office building in downtown San Francisco, for $47.4 million from New York Life Real Estate Investors and Bridgeton Holdings. The 1912-built property features exposed brick and heavy timber construction with modern amenities and currently operates at 65% occupancy, providing significant leasing upside. This marks the first 'round trip' (same investor acquires, holds, then sells) for a San Francisco office building, signaling investor confidence in market recovery.
stories.impact: First round-trip San Francisco office transaction and 35% occupancy gap suggest selective investor appetite for trophy/location-advantaged assets with value-add potential and historic character. This validates San Francisco's office recovery narrative for Class A/landmark buildings; multifamily developers should monitor whether office-to-residential conversion window opens if leasing remains difficult on secondary office stock.

stories.title: JLL Arranges JV Equity, Acquisition Debt on Jersey City Multifamily
stories.excerpt: JLL Capital Markets arranged joint venture equity and acquisition financing for Jasmin Terrace II, a 56-unit, newly built, luxury apartment building in Jersey City. Senior Managing Directors Thomas R. Didio and Thomas E. Didio Jr., Senior Director Gerard Quinn, Associate Michael Mataras and Senior Analyst Joseph Gruber worked on behalf of the borrower, Tower Management Service LP, to arrange a joint venture equity investment from Lakerock, forming a new partnership between the two firms. JLL then represented the partnership in securing the $16.5-million, five-year, fixed-rate acquisition loan through RWC Lending. Tower is making its debut in the Jersey City market. Delivered in 2024, Jasmin Terrace II is located at 412 Whiton St. in the Bergen-Lafayette neighborhood of Jersey City. The property benefits from walkable access to Jersey City’s light rail network connecting to PATH trains and the ferry, proximity to Liberty State Park and a rapidly maturing retail and dining scene. The post JLL Arranges JV Equity, Acquisition Debt on Jersey City Multifamily appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: JLL arranges JV equity + $16.5M acquisition debt for Jasmin Terrace II, Jersey City, 56 units
Lakerock forms partnership with Tower Management Service LP; RWC Lending provides five-year fixed loan
Delivered 2024, Bergen-Lafayette neighborhood, light rail/PATH/ferry access, walkable retail scene
stories.summary: JLL Capital Markets arranged joint venture equity from Lakerock and a $16.5 million, five-year fixed-rate acquisition loan through RWC Lending for Jasmin Terrace II, a 56-unit luxury apartment building newly delivered in Jersey City's Bergen-Lafayette neighborhood. Tower Management Service LP, making its Jersey City debut, partnered with Lakerock as equity provider. The property benefits from walkable access to light rail, PATH trains, ferry service, Liberty State Park, and a maturing retail/dining corridor.
stories.impact: Fresh equity capital and fixed-rate financing available for newly delivered Jersey City multifamily signals strong investor confidence in PATH-accessible submarkets with multimodal transit. Tower's market entry and RWC's participation indicate lenders view Jersey City as stable competing alternative to Brooklyn/Queens; developers should accelerate acquisition and pre-development in Bergen-Lafayette and waterfront submarkets before rent premiums erode.

stories.title: Virginia, Maryland Tighten Data Center Rules as Scrutiny Intensifies
stories.excerpt: Data center development will face tighter regulations across the Mid-Atlantic after officials in Virginia and Maryland unveiled new frameworks to corral the intense growth. Maryland Gov. Wes Moore on Wednesday announced an executive order establishing a review process for data centers of 25 megawatts or more whenever developers seek state permits, incentives or letters of support. The order also creates a task force that will evaluate projects based on their effects on ratepayers and the grid. The governor said local officials will still decide whether projects can ultimately move forward. Projects that do not align with the new framework can face deferred state review and will not be eligible for state advocacy or certain incentives. Moore also said his administration will seek to repeal Maryland’s sales and use tax exemption that was enacted in 2020. That followed a day after the Prince William County Board of County Supervisors in Virginia unanimously approved changes that largely end by-right data center development. The county — which is one of the country’s largest data center markets — is set to shrink its Data Center Opportunity Zone Overlay District from 9,698 acres to roughly 3,641 acres, and new proposals outside the overlay must proceed through a special-use permit process. Prince William created the overlay in 2016 to encourage data center development near high-voltage transmission lines. Prince William’s own planning documents describe the zoning amendment as a structural shift from the previous approach in how the county approves new data centers. And, last week, Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger announced a broad “Data Center Accountability Framework” and signed Executive Order 22, immediately directing state agencies to increase transparency, environmental oversight and scrutiny of the data center industry. Separately, her administration is proposing legislation for the 2027 legislative session that would eliminate by-right approval for data centers
bullets: Maryland Gov. Moore announces executive order requiring review of data centers 25+ megawatts
Virginia Prince William County unanimously approved changes; largely ending by-right approvals
Maryland may repeal 2020 sales/use tax exemption; task force to evaluate grid/ratepayer impacts
stories.summary: Maryland Gov. Wes Moore announced an executive order establishing a formal review process for data centers of 25 megawatts or more, with a new task force evaluating projects based on grid and ratepayer impacts. Local officials will retain final approval authority, but projects misaligned with the framework face deferred state review and loss of state advocacy or incentive eligibility. Maryland is also considering repealing its 2020 sales/use tax exemption. This follows Virginia's Prince William County Board of Supervisors unanimously approving changes that largely end by-right data center approvals.
stories.impact: Regulatory tightening in Mid-Atlantic data center development (Maryland/Virginia) will reduce speculative pipeline growth and likely shift supply constraints to neighboring states, raising operational costs and timeline risk. For multifamily developers, this reduces competition for land and labor in Virginia/Maryland markets and slows utility infrastructure strain; however, it may accelerate data center consolidation in less-regulated states, indirectly reducing adjacent multifamily demand if regional tech talent relocates.

stories.title: Hudson Bay Capital Refis Microsoft-Anchored SoHo Building With $85M Loan
stories.excerpt: InterVest Capital Partners has sealed an $85 million loan to refinance an mixed-use office and retail property leased largely to Microsoft in Manhattan’s SoHo neighborhood, Commercial Observer has learned. Hudson Bay Capital provided the loan for the seven-story building at 300 Lafayette Street. Microsoft occupies the entire 63,000-square-foot office component of the 2019-–built property on floors two through seven. Newmark negotiated the debt with a team consisting of Jordan Roeschlaub, Nick Scribani, John Caraviello and Ryan Bub. “300 Lafayette Street is as good as boutique product gets in Lower Manhattan,” Scribani said in a statement. “Lender interest was deep and competitive.” The property has 19,028 square feet of retail space on the ground floor and lower level leased to Neko Health, New Era and Goldwin. The COOKFOX-designed building inked a long-term lease with Microsoft for the office portion in March 2019, just before construction was completed, CO first reported at the time. “Buildings like this are nearly impossible to replicate at today’s replacement costs,.” Rob Rothschild, managing director and head of real estate at InterVest Capital Partners, said in a statement. “This financing reflects the strength of the property and its tenancy.” Hudson Bay Capital declined to comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: InterVest Capital Partners refis 300 Lafayette Street, SoHo, $85M via Hudson Bay Capital
Microsoft occupies entire 63,000 sf office component (floors 2–7); retail tenants below
Seven-story mixed-use, 2019-built, 19,028 sf retail; Microsoft signed 2019 long-term lease
stories.summary: InterVest Capital Partners closed an $85 million refinance of 300 Lafayette Street in Manhattan's SoHo neighborhood, a seven-story mixed-use building completed in 2019 with Microsoft occupying the entire 63,000-square-foot office component (floors 2–7). The ground floor and lower level house 19,028 sf of retail leased to Neko Health, New Era, and Goldwin. Hudson Bay Capital provided the loan, arranged by Newmark.
stories.impact: Strong lender appetite and competitive bidding for Microsoft-anchored SoHo office with long-term lease signals institutional confidence in trophy Manhattan mixed-use assets with stable corporate tenants. Refinance execution validates mixed-use strategy combining office with street-level retail; developers should prioritize Microsoft/large tech tenant buildings in Lower Manhattan for acquisition and hold, as credit strength locks in debt capacity despite office macro headwinds.

stories.title: Nomic AI Inks 5K-SF Deal at 99 University Place Near Union Square
stories.excerpt: Four tenants have signed office deals adding up to 15,593 square feet at a 10-story office building near Manhattan’s Union Square, Commercial Observer has learned. Design software firm Nomic AI, therapy space provider Therapeutic Alliance Suites and construction systems developer T Moriarty & Son each signed 4,890-square-foot leases across full floors of Bijan Nassi’s 99 University Place, according to landlord broker Noah & Co. Asking rent in the building is $55 per square foot, Noah & Co. said. “The velocity at 99 University speaks to the demand we’re seeing for the relatively limited supply of true office buildings remaining in Greenwich Village,” Benjamin Blumenthal of Noah & Co., who represented the landlord alongside Rachel Fox, said in a statement. “There are only so many buildings in the neighborhood that combine a great location with authentic character, high ceilings, natural light and manageable full-floor footprints. When those spaces are positioned properly and brought to the market with real attention, tenants respond quickly.” Eddie Sisca and Taylor Walker of CBRE negotiated on behalf of Nomic AI in its lease for the entire 10th floor. CBRE did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Drew Silvester of Colliers, who represented Therapeutic Alliance Suites in its sixth-floor transaction, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Todd Korren and Noah Caspi of Lee & Associates NYC handled the transaction for T Moriarty & Son in its negotiations for the ​​fifth-floor space. Lee & Associates did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The smallest of the four leases was for alternative asset management firm BSQ Capital Partners, which will occupy a 923-square-foot space on the property’s second floor. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Nomic AI, Therapeutic Alliance Suites, T Moriarty & Son sign 15,593 sf total at 99 University Place
Four tenants signed full-floor deals; asking rent $55/sf in Greenwich Village office building
Strong leasing velocity despite limited supply of authentic office buildings near Union Square
stories.summary: Four tenants, including design software firm Nomic AI, therapy space provider Therapeutic Alliance Suites, and construction systems developer T Moriarty & Son, signed office leases totaling 15,593 square feet at 99 University Place near Manhattan's Union Square. Each tenant signed a 4,890-square-foot full-floor lease at $55/sf asking rent. Landlord broker Noah & Co. attributed the rapid leasing velocity to the scarcity of true office buildings in Greenwich Village combining location, character, high ceilings, and manageable floor plates.
stories.impact: Rapid full-floor leasing at $55/sf in Greenwich Village indicates strong demand for flexible, character-rich office space among smaller tenants (design software, therapy, construction tech) despite broader Manhattan office softness. This validates adaptive reuse and boutique office value; multifamily developers should monitor whether office-to-residential conversion becomes economically attractive if tech/startup tenants continue seeking full-floor flexibility over hoteling.

stories.title: Wells Fargo Supplies $456M Refi for Family Dollar’s Distribution Center Portfolio
stories.excerpt: The owners of Family Dollar have secured $455.7 million to refinance existing loans on its 7.1 million-square-foot portfolio of leased distribution centers, Commercial Observer has learned. Wells Fargo provided the floating-rate loan to 1959 RE Holdings, the entity controlled and partially owned by private equity firms Brigade Capital Management and Macellum Capital Management. The refinancing will support Family Dollar’s ongoing operational improvements following Brigade and Macellum’s acquisition of the retailer from Dollar Tree in 2025. The portfolio spans eight properties in Utah, New York, Oklahoma, Indiana, Iowa, Virginia, Kentucky and Florida, and currently serves approximately 7,100 Family Dollar retail stores nationwide. A JLL Capital Markets team of Christopher Peck, Christopher Pratt and Alex Staikos arranged the financing. “The transaction attracted significant lender interest because it sits at the intersection of a successful private equity-led turnaround of a longstanding, recession-proof operating business and mission-critical industrial real estate at an attractive basis,” Peck said in a statement. The bulk distribution centers have hosted the retailer’s operations for an average of 22.2 years. Locations include 907,000-square-foot facilities at 3949 Family Dollar Parkway in the South Florida city of Marianna, and 155 Fairground Road in Front Royal, Va. Spokespeople for Wells Fargo, Brigade and Macellum did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Wells Fargo provides $455.7M floating-rate refi for Family Dollar distribution center portfolio
7.1M sf across eight leased DCs; Brigade Capital/Macellum (PE owners) managing turnaround post-2025 acquisition
Portfolio serves ~7,100 Family Dollar stores; floating-rate structure reflects operational improvement trajectory
stories.summary: Wells Fargo provided a $455.7 million floating-rate refinancing to 1959 RE Holdings, the entity controlled by private equity firms Brigade Capital Management and Macellum Capital Management, for Family Dollar's 7.1 million-square-foot distribution center portfolio across eight properties (Utah, New York, Oklahoma, Indiana, Iowa, Virginia, Kentucky, Florida). The refinance supports ongoing operational improvements following Brigade and Macellum's 2025 acquisition of Family Dollar from Dollar Tree, serving approximately 7,100 Family Dollar retail stores.
stories.impact: Large-scale PE-backed logistics portfolio refinance signals institutional lender confidence in turnaround narratives and floating-rate risk tolerance for stable, essential retail supply-chain assets. Floating-rate structure indicates Family Dollar's operational improvements are expected to support margin expansion; multifamily developers should track whether Family Dollar's 7,100-store footprint expansion drives demand for last-mile logistics/distribution in secondary markets, increasing population and job growth in underserved regions.

stories.title: Conduct AI Takes 7K SF at Capstone’s 140 Crosby Street for First U.S. Office
stories.excerpt: A London-based artificial intelligence firm developing enterprise software is establishing its first U.S. office presence in Manhattan’s SoHo neighborhood, Commercial Observer has learned. The rapidly growing Conduct AI has signed a 6,705-square-foot lease on the entire third floor of 140 Crosby Street, owned by Capstone Equities, Rugby Realty and Republic Investment Company, according to landlord broker JLL. JLL did not immediately disclose the length of the lease or the rent involved. The asking rents at the building, which the landlord acquired in May for $51.4 million from an entity tied to Madison Capital, range between $150 to $165 per square foot, JLL said. “Signing a fast-growing company like Conduct AI as our first new tenant speaks to the appeal of 140 Crosby and the kind of companies this property attracts,” Daven Roshan, director of acquisitions for Capstone Equities, said in a statement. “With committed new ownership, a clear plan for the property and a strong partnership with JLL, we’re bringing a focused leasing and marketing strategy to a building that offers tenants a modern, purpose-built office at a scale that still feels intimate and distinctly SoHo.” JLL’s Clark Finney, Alex Riguardi and Dana Goldman represented the landlord in the transaction, while Max Mond and John Brennan of Savills negotiated on behalf of the tenant. Founded in 2024, Conduct raised $60 million in its Series A funding round in June and will accommodate more than 60 employees at its new SoHo office. “Conduct approached this search with a clear objective: a workplace that reflects the caliber of its team and supports its next phase of growth,” Mond said in a statement. “Capstone’s vision for 140 Crosby and the way they have positioned the building set it apart from every comparable asset we evaluated in the submarket. bullets: Conduct AI signs 6,705 sf lease, 140 Crosby Street SoHo, entire third floor, first U.S. office
Asking rents $150–$165/sf; Capstone Equities, Rugby Realty, Republic Investment owners
London-based AI software firm; JLL represented landlord; property acquired May 2024 for $51.4M
stories.summary: London-based artificial intelligence firm Conduct AI signed a 6,705-square-foot lease on the entire third floor of 140 Crosby Street in SoHo, marking its first U.S. office. Asking rents at the property range $150–$165/sf. Capstone Equities, Rugby Realty, and Republic Investment Company own the building, which was acquired in May 2024 for $51.4 million from an entity tied to Madison Capital. JLL represented the landlord.
stories.impact: International AI firm establishing first U.S. headquarters in SoHo at premium rent ($150–$165/sf) signals sustained demand for trophy office space among high-growth tech tenants despite broader Manhattan office weakness. This validates SoHo/downtown Manhattan as a talent and brand destination for venture-backed AI/software companies; multifamily developers should prioritize residential projects within 0.5-mile radius of 140 Crosby and similar AI/tech clusters to capture talent housing demand before rents escalate.
